prose.hook: Oman sits on the Arabian Peninsula between Yemen and the UAE, its territory split into Oman proper and two northern exclaves, Musandam and Al Madhah. Musandam occupies a strategic position right on the Strait of Hormuz, overlooking one of the world's key shipping chokepoints.
prose.physicalGeography: The country's interior is dominated by a central desert plain, flanked by rugged mountains in the north and south. It borders the Arabian Sea, Gulf of Oman, and Persian Gulf.
prose.climate: Oman is dry desert overall, but conditions vary sharply by region: hot and humid along the coast, hot and dry in the interior. The far south catches a strong southwest monsoon between May and September, while summer winds elsewhere can whip up large sandstorms and dust storms, and the country experiences periodic droughts.
prose.economy: Oman runs a high-income, oil-based economy supported by a large welfare system, though government debt has been growing. Policy has focused on favoring citizens in labor force growth and on diversifying the economy beyond oil, alongside a free trade agreement with the US and notably high female labor force participation. Its exports center on crude and refined petroleum, natural gas, semi-finished iron, and fertilizers, with industries spanning oil and gas production, construction, cement, copper, steel, chemicals, and optic fiber.
prose.peopleAndCulture: The population is overwhelmingly Muslim (85.9%), with smaller Christian (6.4%) and Hindu (5.7%) communities. Ethnically, Omanis include Arab and Baluchi populations alongside South Asian communities from India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh, as well as people of African descent.
